summary: Science studies gains its critiques. A new Debate entry, "The Science Wars, 1994–2000", with 23 roster rows (17 new people) and six phase strands, carries critique edges to SSK, Latour, STS, Kuhn and the linguistic turn, and replies into it from SSK, Latour and the history of science; Telling the Truth about History is drawn as a critic of SSK and of Latour, and compared with the Science Wars. Five further critique edges: the 1965–70 critics of Kuhn (science → kuhn), Latour against the strong programme (1992–99), Bloor against Latour (1999), Kuhn against the strong programme (1991), and Trentmann against actor-network theory's view of modernity (consumption → latour, 2009). Roster rows: Laudan as a critic on SSK; Latour and Kuhn as SSK critics linked to their edges; L. Pearce Williams on history of science; Trentmann on consumption. edge_138 is trimmed to the method contrast between programme explanation and laboratory ethnography.
authorization: User, 2026-10-14: "start on the science studies project"; Haraway and Latour are "broadly aligned" (so Haraway is not drawn as a critic of Latour); and "yes" to a new Debate entry "The Science Wars, 1994–2000" (relayed by the coordinating session).
rationale: An outside review (plans/2026-10-13-gemini-review-backlog.md) found that 70 of 166 entries had no critique edge, and that kuhn, latour, ssk, sts and science had none. Research of 2026-10-14 (data/extension-2026/science-studies-critique-2026-10-14/evidence-kuhn-critics.md, evidence-ssk-latour.md, evidence-science-wars.md; data/extension-2026/pathway-endpoints-2026-10-14/evidence-new-materialism.md for Trentmann) read the critics and the replies. The Science Wars attackers (Gross, Levitt, Sokal, Bricmont, Weinberg, Mermin, Koertge) have no atlas home, so only a debate entry can carry their critiques; its participants named the dispute in period (Social Text, 1996), and historians of science intervened on both sides. Edges rest on primary passages read in period texts, on quotations by in-period readers (labelled as such), on publisher abstracts (labelled), and, for Trentmann (2009) and Latour (2004), on dated later work; Higher Superstition, Wise 1996, Latour's Le Monde article and most of A House Built on Sand were not read and are cited only through in-period readers or abstracts. Thin candidates (sciencewars → science, → gender; sts → sciencewars) are not drawn. Canadian-PhD uptake is recorded as metadata only.

edge_138.relationship: offers a comparison between programme-based sociological explanation and laboratory ethnography
edge_138.evidence_note: Comparative teaching link between two methods, not an assertion of a one-way genealogy or of agreement: the Strong Programme's causal and symmetrical explanation of accepted and rejected belief, and Latour and Woolgar's laboratory ethnography of how facts are made. Shared objects do not establish a simple Bloor-to-Latour lineage. The acknowledged debt is edge_685. The disagreement of 1992–99 is carried by the two critique edges of revision 1.135 (latour → ssk and ssk → latour), which hold the Bloor–Latour exchange and its sources.
